what_it_does: This paper describes a driver chip for microscopic OLED displays used in AR/VR headsets that need extremely high pixel density (6285 pixels per inch—finer than the eye can resolve). The core problem: when you build displays this small, the driver circuits must fit in a tiny footprint, and any voltage offset (a small DC shift in the signal) throws off color accuracy. The authors' solution combines three techniques: (1) all pixels share a single automatic calibration circuit that compensates for each column's voltage offset, saving area compared to per-channel calibration; (2) a specially designed output amplifier that can change its slew rate (how fast the voltage swings) to reduce power and noise; and (3) optimized circuit layout to pack everything into just 2,273 square picometers per channel. The result is a compact driver that keeps colors accurate on ultra-dense microdisplays.
